definitions.explanation: free items given as promotional gifts, lottery prizes, or bonus items with purchases

examples.japanese: {抽選|ちゅうせん}で{景品|けいひん}が{当|あ}たった。
examples.english: I won a prize in the lottery.

examples.japanese: {景品|けいひん}を{目当|めあ}てに{買|か}う{人|ひと}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many people buy just to get the promotional gifts.

examples.japanese: この{商品|しょうひん}には{景品|けいひん}が{付|つ}いてくる。
examples.english: This product comes with a free gift.

notes:
FORMATION:
{景|けい} (scene, appearance) + {品|ひん} (item) → gift item (originally items displayed for show)

TYPES OF 景品:
- {抽選|ちゅうせん}{景品|けいひん} (lottery prize)
- {購入|こうにゅう}{特典|とくてん} (purchase bonus)
- ノベルティ (novelty/promotional item)
- おまけ (freebie/bonus - more casual)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {景品|けいひん}が{当|あ}たる (to win a prize)
- {景品|けいひん}を{配|くば}る (to distribute promotional gifts)
- {景品|けいひん}{付|つ}き (with a free gift)

LEGAL CONTEXT:
In Japan, there are regulations called {景品|けいひん}{表示法|ひょうじほう} (Premium Labeling Law) that limit the value of promotional gifts to prevent unfair competition.

RELATED:
- おまけ (bonus item - more casual)
- {賞品|しょうひん} (prize - for competitions)
- {特典|とくてん} (special benefit/bonus)
